# Guideline 5 - Your character has a past Sector Vestige is persistent. Your character is a person with a history, and the shifts they lived through are part of it. We would love to see that history in play: old friends, old rivals, lessons learned the hard way.
## What your character remembers - If your character was alive at the end of a shift, or was revived before it ended, they remember that shift. - If your character died and was still dead when the shift ended, that shift does not carry over for them. - They remember what they saw, heard and learned in character: the people they met, the friendships and rivalries they formed, and who did what, antagonists included. - The usual memory limits of [textlink="Rule 4" link="VestigeRuleR4"] still apply. Anything learned as a ghost, as another character, while unconscious, or outside the game does not count.
## Using your history History is a great reason for roleplay, but it is never a reason to skip [textlink="escalation" link="RuleR11"].
- A grudge from last shift starts at the beginning of escalation, like any other conflict. Words first. - Security should not arrest someone for a past-shift crime on their own initiative. They may keep a closer eye on them, and if security has orders or a warrant to detain that person, acting on it is fine. - Remembering that someone was an antagonist does not make them one now. Unless the game or a GM event tells them otherwise, they are regular crew this shift.
## Examples Good: - Greeting the chemist you worked with yesterday by name and asking how their arm is healing. - Refusing to lend your toolbox to the engineer who set the bar on fire last shift, and telling them why. - As security, remembering that a crewmember was a traitor last shift and watching them more closely. - Two characters picking up a heated argument from last shift, in words.
Not what we are looking for: - Attacking someone at round start because of what they did last shift. - As security, arresting or searching someone for last shift's crimes with no orders or warrant. - Remembering a shift in which your character died and stayed dead. - Calling someone "the traitor from last round" when your character never saw it happen.
